subject.title: Containerized/self-hosted deploys can't use externalized channel plugins: openKeyedStore is gated to trusted plugins, with no supported way to trust a self-hosted channel

question: Should OpenClaw support a separate immutable official-plugin package/provenance root for self-hosted containers, and what checks must it enforce before those external channel plugins receive trusted keyed-state access?
rationale: The source failure is clear, but the fix decides which external code receives host-managed persistent state and channel ingress capabilities, so automation cannot choose the trust model safely.

options.title: Design immutable official-plugin provenance root
options.body: Add a supported build-time/install-time path that preserves official catalog identity, package path, and install records outside the mutable runtime state mount while keeping raw load paths untrusted.

options.title: Document current installer/state-dir contract only
options.body: Keep the existing fail-closed behavior and document that runtime containers must mount the same state directory created by the installer, accepting that common immutable-image layouts remain unsupported.

options.title: Allow explicit local trust override
options.body: Add a config or flag that lets operators trust local/load-path plugins, trading deployment convenience for a broader security boundary that would need strong warnings and tests.

recommendation.title: Design immutable official-plugin provenance root
recommendation.body: Add a supported build-time/install-time path that preserves official catalog identity, package path, and install records outside the mutable runtime state mount while keeping raw load paths untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the live assignee and already stated the relevant official-plugin provenance policy in the issue thread.
